The eviction policy walks the radix tree in insertion order rather than by recency, so hot prefixes get evicted before cold ones.
The scheduler grants memory strictly to whichever request arrived first, without checking whether a higher-priority request is starved indefinitely.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: All tree nodes have refcount > 0 because client requests are paused waiting for memory, creating a circular wait: the allocator waits for requests to finish to evict nodes, but requests wait for the allocator to assign new blocks!
